price_per_million.source: copied from reasoning_models_v1 (confirmed 2026-11-11); thinking tokens billed as output

research_concepts: PNR defensive failure (needs a non-outcome definition)
PULL_UP as a counter play type
league-wide consistency (share of units with lift>0, median lift>2pp)
methodological_questions: How is 'PNR fail' defined without using the possession outcome?
What are the unit, the baseline and the unit of 'lift' (PPP, eFG%, or share)?
Is the 70% / 2pp rule calibrated against a null or permutation distribution given per-unit sampling noise?
Do PBP-derived coverage and play-type labels support defining failure?
Does the effect persist across seasons, and are there multiplicity issues across counters?

historical_evidence.finding: PBP and matchup fields labelled on-ball coverage on only 14.9% (DET) and 3.3% (ORL) of possessions in one game; switches_on was unpopulated. Verdict: failed_gate.

Regular season vs playoffs, PULL_UP PPP allowed changed +0.341 and its possession share fell 7.6pp; PNR share rose 12.1pp, possibly from tagging differences. Records flag LABEL_ERROR and MECHANICAL_FLOOR. No inferential test.

Team-level play-type lifts were small and sometimes negative (ORL vs DET PNR +1.2pp; POR vs SAS PNR -4.1pp). Player-channel lifts were large but on n of roughly 15-54. Failure mechanism A_unanswerable; EXPOSURE_SPARSITY.
Raw turnover-force lifts shrank by about 50% or more once an opponent response was modelled. Net lift was model-implied, not observed, on 4 games.
Defensive play-type edges depended only on the defense (e.g. DAL PNR +9.2% for every offense), so they were not matchup-specific.

Holdout play-type rank validation was supported (median rho +0.539), but the record's failure mechanism is C_artifact: top-3 lift partly reflects league-wide high-efficiency play types, with DRIFT_NONSTATIONARITY flagged.
Year-over-year stability of crunch-time identity was r=-0.023 on 62 pairs; per-unit samples of about 100 possessions leave deltas of +/-0.05 PPP within sampling noise.
Equilibrium and actual-mix matchup predictors had negative R2 versus team means (powered null, B_powered_null) on 520 cells and 69,876 possessions.
An in-game adapter lift did not carry over to Game N+1 (powered null).

failed_approaches.what_failed: Labelling on-ball defensive coverage from NBA matchup and PBP fields
failed_approaches.why: Confident label rates were 3-15%, and switches_on was not populated (LABEL_ERROR, small sample).

failed_approaches.what_failed: Player- and team-level counter lift decomposition on 4 playoff games
failed_approaches.why: Cells held 15-54 possessions, defender attribution included helper steals, and there was no holdout (insufficient exposure).

failed_approaches.what_failed: Treating raw counter lifts as stable
failed_approaches.why: Lifts shrank by about 50% or more after adversarial adjustment, and the net lift was model-implied rather than observed.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Treating small per-unit PPP deltas as a stable team trait
failed_approaches.why: With about 100 possessions per unit, deltas were within sampling noise and year-over-year r was near zero.
R2 was negative against team means in an adequately powered test.

evidence_establishes: No retrieved record directly tests 'after a PNR failure, PULL_UP shows lift>0 in >=70% of units with median >2pp', so that question has not been answered.
Coverage and failure labels derived from PBP and matchup feeds were unreliable in the one game examined (FAM:SF-APPS-058).
Per-unit lift estimates built on about 15-150 possessions were noise-dominated in earlier work (FAM:SF-APPA-066, FAM:SF-APPA-029).
Team-level counter lifts were small, mixed in sign and shrank under adjustment (FAM:SF-APPA-066, FAM:SF-APPA-067).
evidence_does_not_establish: Whether PULL_UP has any true league-wide post-PNR-failure lift.
How large the lift would be, or whether it varies by team or season.
Whether any outcome-independent PNR-failure label can be built from PBP at useful coverage.
Whether the existing derived play-type records tag PULL_UP consistently after a PNR.
own_inferences: If 'fail' is defined from the possession outcome (e.g. a good shot or a score), a PULL_UP lift is partly mechanical or selected, and a positive share would be an artifact.

At about 150 relevant possessions per unit and PPP SD of about 1.1, per-unit SE is roughly 9pp. A true lift of 2pp would give only about 59% of units positive, so the 70% rule effectively requires a true lift of about 5pp or more, and an observed 70% could arise from selection or baseline choice.
PULL_UP may be a high-variance, low-PPP play type, so any lift is baseline-dependent, and regression to the mean is likely if failure is selected on prior poor defensive results.
The 'pp' unit is ambiguous (PPP, eFG% or share) and must be fixed before any analysis.
uncertainties: How the PNR and PULL_UP labels were built in the graph database and their error rates.
Possessions per team-season after a labelled PNR possession.
Whether any non-outcome failure signal (screen navigation, help rotation, shot distance) exists in the data.
No retrieved record addressed this exact claim; relevance came from adjacent studies.

historical_effect.explanation: Without history I might have proceeded with a straightforward unit-level test. The retrieved records show unreliable coverage labels, noise-dominated small-n lifts, shrinkage under adjustment and mechanical-floor/artifact concerns. I therefore require an outcome-independent failure definition, a permutation-calibrated threshold and a pooled estimate, and I treat the 70% rule as noise-prone. No record answered the exact question.

blocking_constraints.text: 'PNR fail' has no outcome-independent definition in PBP and matchup data; defining it by results makes PULL_UP lift partly mechanical.
Per-unit exposure of about 100-200 possessions gives SE of about 8-10pp, so a 70% positive share and 2pp median are mostly noise unless calibrated against a null.
Coverage and play-type labels were unreliable in prior work (FAM:SF-APPS-058, FAM:SF-APPS-012).

prior_work.summary: Retrieved work addresses adjacent issues (coverage labelling, counter lift on small n, stability of small deltas) but none tests PULL_UP lift after PNR failure league-wide. It indicates the test is noise-prone and label-dependent.

risks.text: If failure is defined from the result (made shot, points, foul), PULL_UP lift is conditional on the outcome and not a counter effect.
Defining failure or a weak defense from poor prior results produces regression to the mean in the post-failure comparison.
Per-unit noise makes the share of units with lift>0 hover near 50-60% even with a small true effect.
PULL_UP and PNR tags come from PBP-derived heuristics with unknown precision and recall.
The PNR share jump in FAM:SF-APPS-012 may reflect tagging differences, and coverage labels were sparse.
Shooter quality, defender, shot distance, clock, score and the possession's other actions all affect PULL_UP efficiency.
PULL_UP is a low-frequency, high-variance play type, so the baseline choice determines the sign of lift.
Rule and style changes across 2022-26, and regular season vs playoffs, may change the effect.
The 70% rule has no stated null; the chance rate of positive lift depends on per-unit noise.
Running several counters or definitions of failure inflates false positives unless fixed in advance.

design.estimand: Within-team difference in points per possession between PULL_UP possessions and the team's own non-PULL_UP possessions after a PNR action, matched on context, with 'PNR fail' defined from pre-registered non-outcome features. Lift is in PPP x100 (pp = 0.01 PPP). Primary readouts: pooled lift and the share of units positive, each compared with a permutation null.
design.unit: Offense team-season (regular season, with playoffs analysed separately). Minimum 150 eligible possessions per unit, with a pre-specified exclusion rule.
design.sample: NBA 2022-23 through 2024-25 as the discovery set. 2025-26 regular season (complete from 2026-04-13) as the pre-registered holdout. Playoffs excluded from the primary analysis. Freeze the data version before any analysis.
design.power: At about 150 possessions per unit, SE is about 9pp. Simulate the share of units positive under true lifts of 0, 2, 5 and 8pp before analysis. Accept the 70% rule only if the permutation null puts it well above chance. Pooled power is much higher: roughly 100 units x 150 possessions gives SE of about 1pp.
design.controls: Failure defined without the possession's outcome, from signals such as defender recovery or help distance, if present in PBP. If not possible, stop and report untestable. Adjust for shooter identity and quality, shot distance, clock, score, period, defender, and offense and defense strength. Use a hierarchical model with team random effects. Fix the baseline before any analysis and use an out-of-sample estimate of each team's PULL_UP baseline to limit regression to the mean.
design.falsification: (1) Permutation: shuffle failure labels within team-game to build the null for share positive and median lift. (2) Placebo: replace PULL_UP with other play types such as CUT and SPOT_UP; a similar lift there implies a general effect. (3) Fake-failure: apply the same analysis to PNR possessions labelled 'success' by the same non-outcome rule. (4) Split-half and holdout replication on 2025-26. (5) Label audit on a hand-checked sample of 200 possessions with a stated minimum precision.
design.multiplicity: Single primary hypothesis (PULL_UP after PNR failure). Placebo counters and sensitivity definitions are labelled secondary, with Holm correction across them.
design.decision_rule: Supported only if, on the holdout, the share of units with lift>0 is >=70% and above the permutation 95th percentile, the median lift is >2pp with a bootstrap CI excluding 0 and 2pp, the placebo and fake-failure checks are null, and the label audit passes. If the failure label cannot be defined without outcome information, report untestable. If the pooled lift CI is within +/-2pp of 0, report rejected.
design.data_version: Per-game NBA stats API play-by-play and derived graph play-type records as of 2026-05-23; 2025-26 regular season complete. Record the graph build hash and tagging-script version; do not use partial 2025-26 playoff data.

research_concepts: pull-up jump shot as counter strategy
league-wide counter lift in percentage points
unit-level consistency (share of units with positive lift)
play-type possession records and points per possession
methodological_questions: How is PNR failure defined without using the outcome (outcome-derived label)?
What is the unit of analysis (team, player, team-season) and is there enough exposure per unit?
How is lift computed against a baseline, and does regression to the mean or selection of failure possessions bias it?
Is the 70% of units with lift>0 and median lift>2pp threshold calibrated against a null or placebo distribution?
How are confounders such as shot distance, defender matchup, score, clock and player quality controlled?
Is there multiple testing across counters and seasons, and does the effect hold across seasons (drift)?
args.query: PNR defensive failure then PULL_UP counter lift league-wide share of units positive median lift percentage points

system_prompt:
You are a basketball analytics researcher deciding whether and how a research question should be studied.
You work only from the task statement and the tools listed below. Do not assume facts you have not seen.

The work has two stages, in this order.
Stage 1, retrieval:
1. Read the research objective and the data description.
2. Identify the research concepts and methodological questions the task raises.
3. Retrieve historical evidence by calling retrieve_history.
In stage 1 do not assess the question, predict outcomes or decide. Your only stage-1 reply is the retrieve_history call.
Stage 2, assessment, after the retrieval result is returned:
4. Summarise the relevant historical findings and failed approaches.
5. State what the historical evidence does and does not establish.
6. Assess whether the research question is testable.
7. Identify methodological risks and potential confounders.
8. Make the final research decision.
9. Explain whether and how the historical evidence changed the decision.
The stage-2 output format is given together with the retrieval result.

Evidence rules: keep what a retrieved record states (historical_evidence and failed_approaches, each citing the
identifier of a returned record and its status exactly as recorded) separate from your own inference and from
uncertainty or missing information. Cite only identifiers returned by a tool, and never describe an earlier study that
no tool returned. In some settings retrieval returns no records; then state that no historical evidence was available.

Tools:
- retrieve_history(research_concepts, methodological_questions, query): the prescribed retrieval step. Returns the most relevant consolidated study-family records of earlier research by this project that are available in this setting, with their identifiers; returns an empty list when none are available.
- glossary(): definitions of basketball and project terms used in task statements.
- data_catalog(): the fields available in each per-game data file.
- search_documents(query): rank further study-family documents by text relevance; returns up to 10 families not yet returned.
- read_family(id): the complete record of one study family (for example 'FAM:SF-APPA-001').

Protocol: every reply is exactly one JSON object and nothing else.
To call a tool: {"action": "tool", "tool": "<name>", "args": {...}}
To finish (stage 2 only): {"action": "final", "output": <object following the stage-2 schema>}
You may call at most 12 tools; then you must finish. Check that every opening brace has a closing brace.

Risk codes (use only these): SAMPLE_SIZE_POWER, EXPOSURE_SPARSITY, MEASURE_RELIABILITY, RTM_SELECTION, OUTCOME_DERIVED_LABEL, LEAKAGE_LOOKAHEAD, MECHANICAL_FLOOR, BASE_RATE, CONFOUNDING, LABEL_ERROR, PLACEBO_DEPENDENCE, MULTIPLE_TESTING, IMPLEMENTATION_BUG, DRIFT_NONSTATIONARITY

messages.content:
Research question (as posed on 2026-05-23, in the area of defensive suppression and counter strategy (best/avoid)):
If PNR fail then PULL_UP is a real league-wide counter, it should show lift>0 in >=70% of units with median lift>2pp.

Data available on that date:
- NBA 2022-23 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2023-24 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2024-25 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2025-26 regular season (complete from 2026-04-13; partial before)
- NBA 2025-26 playoffs (complete from 2026-06-21; partial before)
- Sources: Per-game files from the NBA stats API: play-by-play (action type, sub-type, clock, period, score, player, shot distance and result), substitution rotation intervals, starters, defensive matchup minutes and partial possessions, box-score summary. Derived play-type possession records (initiator, play type, points) in a graph database built from the play-by-play.

Your job is to decide, before any analysis is run, whether this question can be answered with this data, what has already been established about it, which methodological and statistical risks threaten a test of it, and either a pre-registration-quality design or a reasoned recommendation not to proceed.

Stage 1. Reply only with the retrieval call: {"action": "tool", "tool": "retrieve_history", "args": {"research_concepts": ["..."], "methodological_questions": ["..."], "query": "..."}}
